blocks.passage:
Customs clearance turns a shipment on paper into goods you can actually sell. It is a small, technical job that feels boring until it goes wrong — and then it is the only thing anyone can talk about for days.

In practice, clearance depends on three things: the right documents, the right classification, and the right values. If any of these is wrong, the shipment can be held, fined, or sent back. Experienced trade teams check every document twice: commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, certificate of origin, and sometimes sanitary or safety certificates.

Customs officers are not the enemy. They are paid to look for problems, and you are paid to make sure they do not find any in your paperwork.

items.q: What does customs clearance turn a shipment into?
items.why: "Customs clearance turns a shipment on paper into goods you can actually sell."

items.q: What three things does clearance depend on?
options: The right documents, classification, and values
items.why: "the right documents, the right classification, and the right values."

items.q: What can happen if one of these is wrong?
options: The shipment can be held, fined, or sent back
items.why: "the shipment can be held, fined, or sent back."

items.q: How do experienced trade teams treat documents?
items.why: "Experienced trade teams check every document twice."

items.q: How does the text describe customs officers?
options: People paid to look for problems, so your paperwork must be clean
items.why: "They are paid to look for problems, and you are paid to make sure they do not find any."

audio.text:
Let me show you this file, because it's a good lesson in what goes wrong. This shipment has been held at customs for three days, and it's entirely a paperwork problem.

Look at the commercial invoice. The HS code here says 0901 — that's roasted coffee. But the goods are actually green, unroasted beans, which is a different code. One wrong number, and the whole classification is off.

Why does it matter? Because the duty rate is different for the two codes. Customs saw a mismatch between the code and the physical goods, and quite rightly, they held it. From their side, it looks like we're either careless or trying to pay less duty.

The fix is simple but slow. We submit a corrected invoice with the right HS code, we pay the correct duty, and once they're satisfied, they release it. But that's three days lost on a one-digit error.

So the lesson: always check the HS code against the actual goods, not against last month's shipment. Every document, twice.

items.q: Why has the shipment been held?
options: It's a paperwork problem — a wrong HS code
items.why: "it's entirely a paperwork problem."

items.q: What was wrong with the HS code?
options: It said roasted coffee but the goods were green, unroasted beans
It was in the wrong language
items.why: "the code here says 0901 — that's roasted coffee. But the goods are actually green, unroasted beans."

items.q: Why does the wrong code matter?
options: The duty rate is different for the two codes
items.why: "the duty rate is different for the two codes."

items.q: What is the fix?
options: Submit a corrected invoice with the right code and pay the correct duty
items.why: "We submit a corrected invoice with the right HS code, we pay the correct duty."

items.q: What is the lesson Charlotte draws?
options: Pay more duty to be safe
Always check the HS code against the actual goods, every document twice
items.why: "always check the HS code against the actual goods, not against last month's shipment. Every document, twice."

items.q: "The **commercial invoice** lists the goods and their value." A commercial invoice is…
options: the seller's bill describing the goods and price
items.why: Commercial invoice = fatura comercial.

items.q: The **bill of lading** is…
options: the document issued by the carrier for the goods shipped
items.why: Bill of lading = conhecimento de embarque.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Customs will **___** the shipment until the code is corrected."
items.why: To hold a shipment = reter a carga.

items.q: The **certificate of origin** shows…
options: the country where the goods were produced
items.why: Certificate of origin = certificado de origem.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Once satisfied, customs will **___** the goods."
items.why: To release = liberar a carga.

items.q: "The shipment got **held up** at customs." To be held up means to…
items.why: Held up = retido, atrasado.

items.q: "Let's **sort out** the paperwork before it ships." To sort out means to…
items.why: Sort out = resolver, arrumar.

items.q: "Double-check the code so nothing **slips through**." To slip through means to…
items.why: Slip through = passar despercebido (um erro).

items.q: "That one-digit error **cost us** three days." To cost someone something means to…
items.why: Cost us three days = custou-nos três dias.

items.q: "Let's **go over** the documents once more." To go over means to…
items.why: Go over = revisar.
